leads.locality: Jardin des Chartreux, Cours du General Giraud, 69004 Lyon
leads.reason: Single source only (the Metropole de Lyon PLU-H remarkable-tree register). Searched the garden's Wikipedia page, its Auvergne-Rhone-Alpes heritage dossier, Vanupied and Office du Tourisme write-ups, and general web search for a hickory/Carya/Caryer specimen in this garden: none corroborate it, and none of them name any walnut-family tree at all. About 280m from the already-published lyo_009 (Garden Trees of Jardin des Chartreux ensemble entry), inside the same garden, which is genuinely promising if a second source ever turns up: an individually locatable specimen would be a stronger entry than the current ensemble one. Also worth fixing the species field before this ever ships: 'Juglans ovoida' is not a real name.

leads.locality: Square Gustave-Auguste Ferrie, angle rue Jacques-Louis Henon et rue Deleuvre, 69004 Lyon
leads.reason: Single source only (the register). Square Ferrie itself is well documented (Ville de Lyon, ruesdelyon.net, mairie4.lyon.fr) as a public garden on the Croix-Rousse plateau, but nothing found names this specific oak, or the neighbouring cedars/beeches at the same square (register_ids 4215, 4216, 4218, 4219), individually. About 800m from lyo_008 (Parc de la Cerisaie), so worth another look if a second source surfaces; the whole square could also be considered as a compact ensemble candidate (a public square with a labelled cedar/oak/beech grouping) rather than one tree, which would need a fresh judgement call under the collectible-point rule. Re-checked 2026-08-20: fetched ruesdelyon.net's own Square Ferrie page directly, it names no individual trees or species at all, only 'une ceinture d'arbres' generically. Still single-sourced, still a lead.
